oneLiner: The sole enabler of leading-edge AI silicon: N2 sold out through 2026, CoWoS 5.5x now in volume production, record monthly revenue running +45% YoY, and a customer base that just guided its own AI demand to $350B over two years.
thesis: Effective monopoly at 2nm-class: N2 entered high-volume manufacturing in Dec 2025, is fully allocated through 2026, and targets ~100K wafers/month by year-end; Intel 18A yields lag to 2027 and Samsung SF2 is still fixing GAA.

HPC - the AI complex of NVIDIA, AMD, Broadcom ASICs and Apple compute - is 66% of revenue and grew 20% QoQ; Broadcom's Sep 2 guide of roughly $115B of FY2027 and $230B of FY2028 AI semiconductor revenue is demand that lands here in wafers and packaging.
2026 revenue growth guided to slightly above 40% YoY in USD with 65-67% gross margins despite overseas-fab dilution; July revenue of NT$467.58B (+44.7% YoY) says the run-rate is ahead of the guide.
Advanced packaging is a second bottleneck TSMC controls: 5.5x-reticle CoWoS entered volume production in August with reported yields above 98% and support for up to twelve HBM4 stacks.

latestQuarter.label: Q2 2026 (Apr-Jun; reported Jul 16, 2026); July revenue reported Aug 10, 2026
points: Revenue $40.2B, +36% YoY, +12% QoQ, at the high end of guidance.
Gross margin 67.7% (above guide); operating margin 60.3%; ADR EPS $4.31, +77% YoY.
Guide: Q3 revenue $44.6-45.8B, gross margin 65-67%; FY2026 growth raised to slightly above 40%.
Node mix: N5 33%, N3 30%, N7 11%, N2 3% (first material quarter); 7nm-and-below is 77% of wafer revenue.
July 2026 revenue NT$467.58B, a record, +44.7% YoY and +5.6% MoM; first seven months NT$2.87T, +37.0% YoY.

segments: HPC 66% of revenue: AI accelerators, custom ASICs, Apple silicon compute.
Smartphone 22%: fall 2026 iPhone silicon on N2 is the next leg.
competitive: Intel 18A reached high-volume manufacturing in late 2025 but Intel concedes world-class yields only by 2027, limiting external foundry wins.
Samsung SF2 is prioritizing GAA yield recovery over leapfrogging.
Reported N2 pricing near $30K per wafer with capacity booked into 2028 (trade press, unverified).

Practically every leading AI accelerator - NVIDIA, AMD, Google TPU, Broadcom XPUs, Trainium, Cerebras - is fabbed here, and Broadcom's own supply commentary named substrates, leading-edge wafers and HBM as its binding constraints, not design capability.
moat: Process leadership plus yield and scale economics, advanced-packaging control, and a customer ecosystem of PDKs, IP and design services that makes defection a multi-year project. N2 was sold out through 2026 before it ramped, and CoWoS capacity - estimated at 120,000-140,000 wafers a month exiting 2026 and expanding again in 2027 - is a second gate that no competitor can open.
risks: Geopolitics: leading-edge concentration in Taiwan remains the structural discount driver, only partly offset by the US-Taiwan trade agreement that cut tariffs on Taiwanese goods to 15% in exchange for $250B of planned Taiwanese investment in the US.
AI capex cyclicality: at 66% HPC, a hyperscaler digestion year hits far harder than in prior cycles.
Customer concentration: Apple historically ~25% of revenue, NVIDIA rising fast, and now Broadcom's XPU ramp adding a third large dependency.
Capex escalation: the $52-56B 2026 plan is reported to be trending as high as $64B as Arizona accelerates, with total US commitment now around $265B (reported, unverified).
Currency: NTD appreciation compresses reported margins (USD revenue, NTD costs).
Smartphone softness: 22% of revenue declined 4% QoQ.
Overseas-fab dilution is structural, not transitory - management already guides gross margin down to 65-67%.
catalysts: August 2026 monthly revenue, due around Sep 10, and each subsequent monthly print.
Q3 2026 results around Oct 15, 2026 with the first 2027 capex framing.
N2 ramp to ~100K wafers/month by end-2026; N2P and A16 progression in 2027.
NVIDIA Rubin volume ramp in Q4 2026 flowing through N3/N2 and CoWoS.
Arizona fab 2 tooling in H2 2026 (mass production H2 2027) and fab 3 pulled toward 2028 for N2/A16.
pricedIn: About $418, roughly 13% below the $479 52-week high: trailing ~35x and forward ~24-26x, well above TSM's own decade norm of mid-teens to 20x forward, because the Taiwan discount has largely compressed out after the stock roughly doubled in a year. The multiple embeds 40%+ 2026 growth plus a healthy 2027. Debate: are 60%+ operating margins peak-cycle artifacts, and does an AI capex pause turn a structural re-rating back into a cyclical one? Against that, Broadcom just underwrote roughly $350B of two-year AI silicon demand that has to be fabricated and packaged somewhere, and there is only one somewhere.

scenarios.bear: Hyperscaler capex digests in 2027 just as record capacity lands; HPC growth stalls; overseas costs, a capex bill running toward $64B and NTD strength pull gross margin to the high 50s; the multiple mean-reverts toward ~18x forward on renewed geopolitical pricing.
scenarios.base: 2026 closes at 40%+ growth as guided, with monthly prints running ahead of it; N2 ramps to ~100K wafers/month at premium pricing and CoWoS expands into 2027; growth slows but stays healthy in 2027; gross margin holds mid-60s; the stock tracks earnings at low-to-mid-20s forward.
scenarios.bull: N2 pricing power plus a monopoly-like leading edge while rivals slip; accelerator unit growth compounds through Rubin, MI400 and the Broadcom XPU ramp, all fabbed here; packaging stays the scarce good and carries near-7nm ASPs; margins hold at records and the market pays a sustained premium for the sole enabler of the AI build-out.

valPresets.note: Valuation basis is forward earnings, not FCF: TTM FCF is structurally depressed by a capex program of $52-56B and rising, which would make an FCF-DCF read absurdly demanding.

notes: Statement history shown is 4 years (Yahoo) because TSMC files 20-F/6-K rather than 10-K/10-Q; figures converted from TWD at spot. FCF here is capex-heavy: the valuation lab base case uses normalized growth off a depressed FCF base.
latestProse: Q2 2026 (reported Jul 16). Revenue $40.2B (+36% YoY, +12% QoQ), at the high end of guidance. Gross margin 67.7% (+150bp QoQ, above guide), operating margin 60.3%, ADR EPS $4.31 (+77%). Platform mix: HPC 66% of revenue (+20% QoQ), smartphone 22% (-4% QoQ). Node mix: N5 33%, N3 30%, N2 3% - the first material N2 quarter - with 77% of wafer revenue at 7nm and below. July revenue, reported Aug 10, was a record NT$467.58B, +44.7% YoY and +5.6% MoM, taking the first seven months to NT$2.87T (+37.0%). The disclosure that matters most: N2 at 3% of revenue in its first material quarter, against capacity already sold out - the mix shift to the highest-ASP node has barely started.
guidanceProse: Q3 guide is $44.6-45.8B with gross margin 65-67% and operating margin 56-58%; FY2026 growth stands at slightly above 40% in USD, and the July run-rate is tracking ahead of it. Capex was planned at $52-56B and trade press now reports it trending as high as $64B as Arizona accelerates - fab 2 (N3) complete and tooling in H2 2026 for H2 2027 production, fab 3 pulled toward 2028 for N2 and A16, and another $100B committed, taking total US commitment to roughly $265B. The margin guide-down reflects overseas-fab dilution plus NTD strength. On packaging, 5.5x-reticle CoWoS entered volume production in August at reported yields above 98%, supporting up to twelve HBM4 stacks.
